title: I tried the GPT-6 cheetah challenge with a reference video. Here’s what it produced.
author: bGivenb
selftext:
Saw [the “GPT-6 Astra is definitely NOT AGI” post](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1w7m5fn/gpt6_astra_is_definitely_not_agi/) and wanted to try the same kind of task with a different workflow.

The original prompt asked it to rig and animate a cheetah at AAA/Hollywood quality. I gave it a visual reference and asked it to build a way to check its own work.

Here’s everything I did:

1. Asked Codex to find a free cheetah model and download it.
2. Took a screenshot of the unanimated model.
3. Pasted that screenshot into Grok and asked it to generate a video of the cheetah running.
4. Gave that video to GPT-6 in Codex with this prompt:

>

Then I just let it work. I didn’t manually rig anything, adjust keyframes, or send corrective follow-up prompts.

It extracted reference frames, built the rig, animated the model, and wrote scripts to render and compare its progress. It caught and corrected problems with the floor, skin weights, and limbs shrinking during interpolation.

The result is an editable Blender scene with a six-second animation and 31 rig controls. **The comparison video shows Grok’s reference on the left and the Blender render on the right.**

There’s still some rubbery deformation, and it needs cleanup. But honestly, this is almost usable. 

Model credit: [Cheetah by Poly by Google](https://poly.pizza/m/5y59KqZXxWf), CC BY 3.0.
